discovery: Programmable arrays of individually trapped Rydberg atoms for quantum simulation and quantum information processing

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire Charles Fabry, Institut d'Optique Graduate School, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum optics
motivation: The nominees turned the strong interactions between Rydberg atoms into a controlled resource for many-body quantum physics. Lukin proposed the Rydberg blockade as a mechanism for quantum gates and collective entanglement. Saffman and Browaeys first demonstrated blockade between two single atoms held in optical tweezers (2009), then realised deterministic entangling gates. Browaeys and Lukin then built defect-free, reconfigurable arrays of hundreds of atoms. These arrays have realised quantum Ising and XY magnets, observed quantum phase transitions and many-body scars, prepared topological spin liquids, and run error-corrected logical qubits. With single-atom control and single-site readout, a quantum many-body system can now be assembled atom by atom, measured, and followed as it becomes entangled and decoheres. The field grew out of cavity-QED and Rydberg physics, and it has become one of the leading platforms both for testing quantum theory and for quantum technology.
